5.text: The girls of the Chukchee have small lamps and dishes, and dolls of

6.text: various sizes (Fig. 198, a, b), sometimes almost as big as a very small baby.

7.text: The dolls have clothes that are carefully made, and represent grown persons

8.text: and children of both sexes. The favorite one is that representing a small

9.text: infant wearing a diaper and baby-clothes. Some of the dolls pass by inheritance

10.text: from generation to generation. They are even supposed to be connected with

12.text: The women and children are fond of making figures by skilfully winding

13.text: loops of thread around the fingers of both hands. The game is called yuˊᵋut,

14.text: and is somewhat analogous to cat’s-cradle of civilized people. It exists among

15.text: the Eskimo tribes of America, and is mentioned by Boas as occurring among

16.text: the Central Eskimo,¹ and by Kroeber among the Eskimo of Smith Sound.²

17.text: In Asia it existed among the Chukchee from the Kolyma to the Pacific coast.

18.text: In former times it was also known among the Kamchadal and the Koryak.
